title: Home
text: Boone Bowles Assistant Professor of Finance Adam C. Sinn '00 Department of Finance Mays Business School | Texas A&M University Email: boone.bowles@tamu.edu Curriculum Vitae I research asset pricing and institutional investors, with projects on stock-market anomalies, mutual funds, short selling, information acquisition, and financial social media. I teach corporate finance in Mays Business School's full-time MBA, engineering MBA, and flex-online MBA programs. I also created Boone's Finance Boot Camp , a public, self-paced finance fundamentals curriculum. I received my Ph.D. in finance from the University of North Carolina's Kenan-Flagler Business School. I earned an M.S. in financial economics and a B.S. in economics from Utah State University's Jon M. Huntsman School of Business. I like to exercise, read, and be with my wife and children.

title: Teaching
text: Teaching Innovations Boone’s finance boot camp Boone’s finance boot camp is a public, self-paced finance fundamentals curriculum featuring 19 short instructional videos, companion notes, Excel workbooks, interactive calculator tools, and auto-graded quizzes drawn from large question banks with immediate explanatory feedback. VB—Virtual Boone, an LLM-powered teaching assistant trained on the Boot Camp materials, provides students with individualized support. The curriculum covers time value of money, bonds, financial statements, free cash flow, and NPV. The project was developed through the Montague–Center for Teaching Excellence Scholar Award. Flex-online MBA core finance curriculum development Selected to design and launch the eight-week core finance course for Mays Business School’s Flex-Online MBA program. Built the course around financial valuation, integrating synchronous and asynchronous instruction, applied assignments, and interactive learning tools. title: Corporate Finance (MBA)
text: FINC 612: Corporate Finance -- Full-Time and Engineering MBA Firms face important questions: Will the proposed project create or destroy value? Should we invest in robotics or enhance our labor force? Given limited resources, which of several projects should we select? How should we fund the expansion of our facilities? To answer these questions, firms quantify the effects of their decisions on firm value. In this course, we focus on fundamental financial concepts and develop skills in valuation to address these important questions. This course is intensive; we not only seek to understand financial concepts but work diligently to acquire important tools. Next Offering Fall 2026 Previous Syllabi Fall 2025 , Fall 2024 , Fall 2022 , Fall 2021

title: Money & Capital Markets
text: FINC 381: Money & Capital Markets This course examines money, financial markets, and financial institutions. The first half of the course covers interest rates, the Federal Reserve, monetary policy, and financial crises. The second half explores markets, financial instruments, banking, and other relevant topics. This course demands analytical thinking and the application of economic concepts.
